terms.gloss: the pivot of a door, a hinge
evidence: Verg. A. 1.449: foribus cardō strīdēbat aēnīs
terms.comment: A Roman door turned on pivots set in sockets above and below; the word serves for any hinge. A door opened is versō cardine. A hinge that squeaks strīdet (see “screech”); to oil it is cardinem ungere, as Cato greases axles and leather with boiled-down olive lees. By a figure, the point on which everything turns (see “crucial”).

phrases.english: The hinge squeaks; let’s oil it.

phrases.latin: vidēn' ut aperiuntur aedēs fēstīvissumae? num muttit cardō? est lepidus.
phrases.english: Do you see how the lovely house is opening? Does the hinge make a sound? It’s a charming one.

phrases.latin: aere trabēs, foribus cardō strīdēbat aēnīs
phrases.english: its beams bound with bronze, the hinge creaked on the bronze doors

phrases.latin: Amurcā dēcoctā axem unguitō et lōra et calciāmenta et coria; omnia meliōra faciēs.
phrases.english: Grease the axle with boiled-down olive lees, and the straps, the shoes, and the hides; you will make them all better.

sources: Lewis & Short: cardo · Lewis & Short: ungo · Lewis & Short: amurca
